task: Align Dockerfile builder to Go 1.26, pin the full apk closure in both stages, and gate the Dockerfile build in CI before release (#26)

events.summary: Scoped to the Dockerfile (builder FROM line, both apk add lines), a new image-build job in .github/workflows/ci.yaml, and this trace file. go.mod (go 1.26.0), ci.yaml's existing go-version/go-version-input pins, the chart's appVersion, release.yaml, and application code were confirmed already correct or out of scope and left untouched. A second-opinion supply-chain review of the first pass requested two corrections, both applied: (1) pin the full transitive closure apk installs in each stage, not just the named top-level packages; (2) add a CI job that builds the Dockerfile for every release.yaml platform before a release tag is pushed, since no existing job did. Its first CI run then exposed one narrowly-scoped egress/input correction: Docker Hub redirected the QEMU binfmt blob to production.cloudfront.docker.com, absent from the allowlist, and setup-qemu-action still used its mutable default binfmt:latest. This follow-up adds only that CDN host and pins the QEMU image to its Docker Hub multi-arch manifest-list digest. The next CI build correctly exposed a stale builder-closure pin (`pcre2=10.47-r1`); the live Alpine 3.24 index now supplies pcre2=10.48-r0 required by the still-pinned git=2.54.0-r0, so this follow-up refreshes only that closure member.

Directly observed the three problems this change fixes. (1) Toolchain drift: the Dockerfile builder was golang:1.27-alpine while go.mod declared `go 1.26.0` and every go-version/go-version-input pin in .github/workflows/ci.yaml was already '1.26' -- read directly from all three files, a real and verifiable inconsistency, not a hypothetical one. (2) Non-reproducible apk installs: the runtime and builder apk add lines named only the top-level packages (xfsprogs-extra, quota-tools, e2fsprogs, util-linux, btrfs-progs; git in the builder), while the digest-pinned base images left every transitive dependency -- 60 additional runtime packages, 11 additional builder packages -- resolving from the still-mutable Alpine 3.24 apk index on each rebuild; confirmed by extracting P:/V: pairs from /lib/apk/db/installed in the bare digest-pinned base images (alpine:3.24@sha256:28bd5f..., golang:1.26-alpine@sha256:b6890e...) and diffing against the same file in images built with only the five/one named packages installed -- 65 and 12 packages respectively existed in the built image but not the bare base, none of them version-pinned. (3) No pre-release build gate: neither ci.yaml nor release.yaml ran `docker build` anywhere before release.yaml's build-and-push job, which only runs on a pushed release tag -- confirmed by reading both workflow files -- so a dependabot digest bump landing on an Alpine point release that dropped one of these pins would stay green through every existing CI job and fail only after the tag was already pushed.

Fixed all three. (1) Builder FROM changed from golang:1.27-alpine@sha256:4c9fe601... to golang:1.26-alpine@sha256:b6890e35ded5d19118c2bca3d7754dc4e6f694aac2d0aeb92f9807c2879e4230, the multi-arch manifest-list digest (covers linux/amd64, arm64, arm/v6, arm/v7, 386, ppc64le, riscv64, s390x; resolves to Go 1.26.8 on alpine3.24), resolved via `docker buildx imagetools inspect golang:1.26-alpine` on 2026-09-02. (2) Both apk add lines now pin the full closure computed as (packages in the built image) minus (packages in the bare digest-pinned base), one `name=version-release` per line, sorted: 65 lines on the runtime stage (xfsprogs-extra, quota-tools, e2fsprogs, util-linux, btrfs-progs and every package apk pulled in for them, e.g. libuuid, python3, linux-pam), 12 on the builder stage (git and its closure, e.g. libcurl, libidn2, nghttp2-libs). The new image-build job caught the intended loud failure when the mutable Alpine 3.24 index removed its stale pcre2=10.47-r1 closure member: pcre2=10.48-r0 is now required by the still-pinned git=2.54.0-r0. Refresh only that one builder closure pin; all other package pins and both base digests remain unchanged. (3) Added an `image-build` ("Image Build") job to ci.yaml that runs on every push/PR: docker/setup-qemu-action + docker/setup-buildx-action + docker/build-push-action build the Dockerfile for linux/amd64, linux/arm64 and linux/arm/v7 (the same three platforms release.yaml's build-and-push job targets) with push:false, load:false, cache-from/cache-to type=gha. The first run failed before Buildx because its default `docker.io/tonistiigi/binfmt:latest` blob redirected to `production.cloudfront.docker.com`, which was absent from the allowlist. The follow-up adds only that Docker Hub CDN endpoint and sets setup-qemu-action's image to `tonistiigi/binfmt@sha256:400a4873b838d1b89194d982c45e5fb3cda4593fbfd7e08a02e76b03b21166f0`, the multi-arch manifest-list digest returned by Docker Hub's official tag API on 2026-09-02. Decision D5 (#26) then reverted the apk version pins entirely, both in this stage and the runtime stage below: Alpine stable keeps only the current version of each package in its index, so a version pin breaks on every upstream bugfix release, not just a real regression -- 'fail loudly on drift' became 'fail constantly', and the PR-time Image Build job would have blocked unrelated PRs on routine Alpine churn. Both apk add lines are back to bare package names (`git`; `xfsprogs-extra quota-tools e2fsprogs util-linux btrfs-progs`), and the digest-pinned FROM lines plus the Go 1.26 builder alignment are untouched. The runtime stage's manifest-recording step changed from `apk info -a` on the five named packages (license text only) to `apk info -v | sort > /licenses/os-packages-manifest.txt` (81 lines: every installed package, base plus closure, with version), making the manifest the build-time record of exactly what the reverted pins used to freeze. The comment above the runtime apk add line was rewritten to state the reproducibility boundary honestly: base digests and go.sum are frozen inputs, apk packages resolve from the live index and are RECORDED not frozen, the primary provenance record for OS package versions is the Syft-based SBOM release.yaml's build-and-push job generates (`sbom: true` on the docker/build-push-action step) plus this manifest, and the Image Build job still catches a package disappearing entirely -- just not a version changing under it.

The Dockerfile builder had drifted one Go minor version ahead of go.mod and every CI go-version pin, and apk installs in both stages were not reproducible: of the 77 packages apk actually installed across the two stages (65 runtime + 12 builder), none were version-pinned before this change, so they resolved from a live, mutable index on every rebuild despite the base image itself being digest-pinned. Fixed by realigning the builder digest to golang:1.26-alpine (1.26.8-alpine3.24) and pinning every package in the closure apk actually installs in each stage -- computed via `apk info -v` / `/lib/apk/db/installed` diffed against each stage's bare base image, not guessed -- plus adding the image-build CI job so a future base-digest bump that drops one of these pins from the Alpine index is caught on the next PR instead of after a release tag is pushed.

Post-D5: `docker build --no-cache -t nfs-quota-agent:d5-check .` (native arm64 on this colima host) succeeded end to end with both apk add lines back to bare package names. `docker run --rm --entrypoint cat nfs-quota-agent:d5-check /licenses/os-packages-manifest.txt | wc -l` printed 81 (the full installed set: 16 bare alpine:3.24 base packages + 65 closure packages), confirming the manifest now records every installed package with version, not just the five requested tools; grep -i pcre2 on that manifest found nothing (pcre2 is builder-stage-only). A separate `--target builder` build confirmed the builder stage's unpinned `apk add git` resolves cleanly against the live index, installing pcre2-10.48-r0 -- the same version that broke the reverted pin -- with no error. `python3 scripts/ci/check-mutable-inputs.py .github/workflows/ci.yaml .github/workflows/release.yaml .github/workflows/agent-behavior.yml` printed 'Mutable-input guard passed for 3 file(s)'. `make test` passed with zero FAIL lines across all packages.
events.scope: Dockerfile apk-unpinned build correctness and full-manifest recording on the colima docker context (aarch64 native); does not exercise quota enforcement, which this change does not touch

events.summary: Verified the closure-pinned Dockerfile and the new CI job's target platform set work on linux/arm/v7, previously unexercised for this Dockerfile and not natively supported by the colima buildx builder (which only listed linux/arm64, linux/amd64, linux/amd64/v2, linux/386). Installed QEMU emulation with `docker run --privileged --rm tonistiigi/binfmt --install all`, which added linux/arm/v7 (and v6) to the supported platform list. `docker buildx build --platform linux/arm/v7 --no-cache -t nfs-quota-agent:armv7-check --load .` then succeeded end to end, including the Go build step running under QEMU emulation and all 65 runtime apk pins installing without a single version-resolution error. `docker run --platform linux/arm/v7 --rm --entrypoint apk nfs-quota-agent:armv7-check info -v` showed btrfs-progs-6.17.1-r1, e2fsprogs-1.47.4-r0, quota-tools-4.11-r0, util-linux-2.42.1-r0 and xfsprogs-extra-7.0.1-r0 -- the identical pinned versions seen on amd64/arm64, confirming the pins are not architecture-specific and the same Alpine index resolution holds across arches. Separately confirmed via the Docker Hub registry API (bearer token obtained from auth.docker.io, manifest fetched from registry-1.docker.io with an OCI image-index Accept header) that the golang:1.26-alpine manifest list includes a linux/arm/v7 platform entry alongside amd64, arm64, arm/v6, 386, ppc64le, riscv64 and s390x, so the new builder base itself supports the third platform the new image-build CI job and release.yaml both target. These specific version pins (65 runtime, 12 builder) were later reverted per D5 (#26): the live Alpine 3.24 index dropped pcre2=10.47-r1 within hours of this verification, reproduced identically on linux/arm64 and with the plain unpinned `docker build`, proving it was index churn, not a pin-mechanism defect. See the new post-D5 reproduction and regression_verification events below for the unpinned build's evidence.
events.scope: arm/v7 build correctness and apk pin version parity under QEMU emulation on the colima docker context, plus the golang:1.26-alpine base image's platform coverage confirmed independently via the Docker Hub registry API

events.summary:
Reproduced the pcre2 churn D5 is a response to. `docker buildx build --platform linux/arm/v7 ...` and, separately, a native `docker build --target builder` both failed identically with the still-pinned builder closure: `ERROR: unable to select packages:
  pcre2-10.48-r0:
    breaks: world[pcre2=10.47-r1]
    satisfies: git-2.54.0-r0[so:libpcre2-8.so.0]`. The same failure reproduced on linux/arm64 (native) and with the plain unpinned `docker build` (no buildx, no driver pin), ruling out the buildx buildkit digest pin or the target platform as the cause: the Alpine 3.24 index itself had moved pcre2 from 10.47-r1 to 10.48-r0 between an earlier successful build this session and this one, and Alpine stable does not keep the superseded version available -- there was no index entry left to satisfy the old pin at all, only a newer one git's shared-library dependency now required.

Post-D5 (pins removed, manifest records the full closure): `docker build --no-cache` succeeded on native linux/arm64 and on linux/amd64 (isolated apk-only Dockerfile, since a full linux/amd64 build independently fails at the unrelated `go mod download` step under this host's QEMU amd64 emulation -- a pre-existing Go-runtime-under-QEMU HTTP/2 crash reproduced identically before and unrelated to any change in this PR, not caused by D5), and `docker buildx build --platform linux/arm/v7 --no-cache --load` succeeded end to end including the full Go build. On all three, `/licenses/os-packages-manifest.txt` was exactly 81 lines (16 bare alpine:3.24 base packages + 65 closure packages, byte-for-byte the same set as the earlier closure-pin work), and `grep -i pcre2` on that runtime manifest found nothing (pcre2 belongs to the builder stage's git closure, not the runtime image). The builder stage's now-unpinned `apk add git` was separately confirmed, via `--target builder`, to resolve pcre2-10.48-r0 -- the exact version that broke the reverted pin in e7 -- cleanly, with no error, proving the unpinned approach survives the index churn that broke the pinned one.
events.scope: Post-D5 build correctness (amd64, arm64, arm/v7) and full-closure manifest recording across architectures on the colima docker context; does not exercise quota enforcement, which this change does not touch

events.summary: #26's supply-chain-hardening scope is done within the scope stated in e1 and at the evidence level in e5, e6 and e8: the Dockerfile builder matches go.mod and CI at Go 1.26 via a multi-arch manifest-list digest; a new CI job builds the Dockerfile for all three release platforms on every PR so a package disappearing from the Alpine index entirely is caught before a release tag is pushed; and, per decision D5, apk package versions are deliberately NOT pinned (base digests and go.sum remain the frozen inputs) because Alpine stable's index does not retain superseded versions, so a version pin breaks on every routine upstream bugfix rather than only on drift worth blocking a PR over. The full installed closure (81 packages) is instead recorded in /licenses/os-packages-manifest.txt at build time, with the Syft-based SBOM release.yaml's build-and-push job generates as the primary OS-package provenance record -- verified reproducible and identical across amd64, arm64 and arm/v7.

Complete at the build, Go-1.26-toolchain-alignment, CI-existence-gate, full-closure-manifest-recording, cross-arch-parity and unrelated-test-suite level. Explicitly NOT attempted: apk version pinning, which was tried, found to break on routine Alpine index churn, and deliberately reverted per D5 -- this is a considered scope boundary, not something left outstanding.
